 Oral Judgment

(PER: THE HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE VENKATESH NAIK T) The appellants - claimants have filed this appeal challenging the judgment and award dated 05.09.2013 passed by the MACT II,
Bagalkote in M.V.C. No.345/2012 [for short, 'the Tribunal'], whereby the Tribunal dismissed the petition filed by the claimants.
2. For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to as per their ranks before the Tribunal.
3. Brief facts of the case are that on 12.03.2012, the deceased Muttappa S/o. Parasappa Asangi was returning to his Gudur village via Ron after attending Urs at Yamanur village in tomtom goods autorickshaw bearing registration No.KA- 29/7354 and when the said tomtom goods autorickshaw proceeding in between Hirehal and Jalihal village at about 07:30 p.m. slowly, at that time, the driver of KSRTC bus bearing registration No.KA-23/F-603 while coming from opposite direction drove the same in rash and negligent manner and while overtaking one tractor, which was also coming from opposite direction of the said tomtom goods NC: 2024:KHC-D:18076-DB autorickshaw, dashed against the said tomtom goods autorickshaw and as a result, tomtom goods autorickshaw turtled and the deceased sustained injuries and succumbed to the injuries on the spot.
4. The claimants in order to prove their claim examined on oath as PWs.1 to 3 and relied upon Exs.P1 to P8.
For the defence, the driver of the KSRTC bus was examined on oath as RW1.
Considering oral and documentary evidence on record, the Tribunal dismissed the claim petition.
5. Learned counsel for the claimants vehemently contended that the Tribunal has not framed issues properly and not given any findings on the issues framed.
The Tribunal has failed to note that the FIR was registered against the driver of the KSRTC bus and hence, the materials placed on record to prove the negligence on the policy of the driver.
Therefore, the Tribunal ought not to have dismissed the claim petition filed by the appellants - claimants.

6. On the other hand, the other claimants arising out of the same accident have filed the claim petitions in M.V.C. NC: 2024:KHC-D:18076-DB No.114/2015 and M.V.C. No.115/2015 and the Tribunal has saddled the responsibility on the respondent - Corporation.

Therefore, the Tribunal Smt. Hanamavva W/O Muttappa Asangi vs The Divisional Manager on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/2788294/

sentences.text: 7. Heard the learned counsel for the parties.
Perused the judgment and award of the Tribunal.
8. It is not in dispute that the deceased Muttappa met with road traffic accident on 12.03.2012 and due to the injuries sustained in the accident, he died on the spot.

9. Arising out of the same accident, the claim petitions filed by the claimants in MVC No.114/2015 &
MVC No.115/2015, a co-ordinate Bench of this Court in MFA No.103777/2018 & MFA No.100623/2018 has saddled entire liability on the Corporation to pay compensation.
However, the Tribunal, in the instant case, has not answered issue No.2 framed with regard to the age, avocation and income of the deceased.
This aspect is not disputed by the learned counsel for the Corporation.

In the last and in the alternative, the learned counsel has argued that if at all this Court found the want of requisite evidence, the proper course is to exercise the power of remand under the provisions of Order XLI Rule 23-A CPC.

The learned counsel has contended that this Court being the first Court of Appeal, must give an opportunity to the appellants/claimants to adduce proper additional evidence, considering the fact that the finding of the Tribunal was against them.

11. A conjoint reading of Rules 23, 23A and 24 of Order XLI brings forth the scope as also contours of the powers of remand that when the available evidence is insufficient to dispose of the matter, the proper course for an Appellate Court is to follow the mandate of Rule 24 of Order XLI CPC and to determine the real questions in controversy between the parties finally.
12. It is only in such cases where the decree/award in challenge is reversed in appeal and a re-trial is considered necessary that the Appellate Court shall adopt the course of remanding the case.

In this case, the appellants/claimants NC: 2024:KHC-D:18076-DB pleaded that the Tribunal in the aforesaid claim petitions based on the materials produced by the claimants has awarded compensation and this Court in MFA No.103777/2018 & MFA No.100623/2018 has rightly saddled entire liability on the Corporation and enhanced the compensation in respect of the claimants therein.

Under such circumstances, this Court is of the considered view that in the interest of justice and equity, retrial is necessary, inasmuch as co-ordinate Bench of this Court in the aforesaid MFAs taking note of the evidence on record has rightly saddled entire liability on the Corporation and enhanced compensation in respect of the claimants therein.

13. Therefore, to give one more opportunity to both the parties to adduce their respective evidence in support of their claims, we are of the view that the matter requires to be remanded for fresh consideration keeping in view of the observations made in M.F.A. No.103777/2018 and M.F.A.
No.100623/2018 [arising out of the above two claim petitions M.V.C. Nos.114/2015 and 115/2015]
passed by the Co- ordinate Bench of this Court.

Accordingly, we proceed to pass the following:
NC: 2024:KHC-D:18076-DB ORDER i.
Appeal is allowed.
